studies.headline: Corvus albicollis occupies about as much of the region as it did thirty years ago.
studies.value: -0.016 in the probability a cell is occupied
studies.detail: Occupancy 0.496 in 1987-1991 against 0.480 in 2008-2012, over 496 quarter-degree cells atlassed at least 20 times in both epochs. Detection was estimated separately in each epoch at 0.222 and 0.261.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.

rows.label: Reporting rate, uncorrected
rows.detail: 0.496 to 0.480 — the share of cells the bird was seen in at all, which is what the answer would have been without a detection model

rows.label: Against the other five-year window
rows.detail: 2019-2023 in place of 2008-2012, and the sign agrees

studies.caveat: Absence of a result is not a result. This says the data cannot answer the question, not that the answer is no.

studies.headline: Hirundo rustica was recorded almost everywhere in both atlases, so no change can be measured.
studies.detail: Where a species is found in nearly every cell, how often it is missed cannot be estimated, and occupancy cannot be told apart from one. Registered in advance as an outcome rather than discovered as a problem.
studies.caveat: Two atlases thirty years apart, so this is a before and after and not a trend: nothing here is per decade. South Africa, Lesotho and Eswatini only, and only where volunteers atlassed twice. Nothing here says why.
